description: Photograph of four armed fighters in camouflage with faces covered by balaclavas and scarves, posing before a large black banner painted with the ISIS shahada design. Two of them hold up a red Antifaschistische Aktion (Antifa) flag in front of the banner. The fighters carry AK-pattern rifles and ammunition belts; the setting is a dusty roundabout in an arid town, consistent with widely circulated images of international volunteers with Kurdish YPG/IFB forces in northern Syria posing at a captured ISIS billboard. The specific individuals and town are not identified.
text: ANTIFASCHISTISCHE AKTION. [Arabic on banner:] لا إله إلا الله [there is no god but God]. الله رسول محمد [seal: God, Messenger, Muhammad].
flags: Fighters are masked and unidentified; location and unit inferred from context, not shown in the image
Circulated in Q-adjacent posts to link Antifa with ISIS; the original context (anti-ISIS volunteers at a captured banner) is disputed by that framing

description: Close-up photograph of a collection of U.S. military and aerospace patches arranged on a dark case. At top is a subdued 4th Infantry Division shoulder patch above a black Operation Iraqi Freedom Veteran patch with an embroidered campaign ribbon. Below are three round patches: a red-and-black B-2 Combined Test Force patch, a 419th (Flight Test Squadron) Ops Engineering patch showing a jester, wizard and clown with the motto Stuck In The Middle, and a Northrop Grumman/Raytheon Global Hawk program patch (CVCE GH RUN DEMO with MP-MCS and CMCC elements). A small gold letter-Q charm and a second small gold pin rest on the patches. Referenced by Q post 4695; the photo presents the patches as evidence of the poster's military/flight-test background.
text: OPERATION IRAQI FREEDOM. VETERAN. B-2. COMBINED TEST FORCE. 419th OPS ENGINEERING. STUCK IN THE MIDDLE. GHOC · CMMS · AFRCO. MP-MCS. CMCC. NORTHROP GRUMMAN. Raytheon. CVCE GH RUN DEMO.
flags: Some ring text on the Northrop Grumman patch is partly obscured; GHOC/AFRCO reading is best-effort

description: Screenshot of a verified @realDonaldTrump tweet from May 31, 2020 stating that the United States will designate ANTIFA a terrorist organization. The embed shows 380K likes and a footer noting 192K people are talking about this, in the style of a Twitter embed on a news page.
text: Donald J. Trump. @realDonaldTrump. The United States of America will be designating ANTIFA as a Terrorist Organization. 380K. 4:23 PM - May 31, 2020. 192K people are talking about this.
flags: The tweet announces an intention; no formal federal terrorist-organization designation of Antifa followed under existing law

Elements include selfies, photos of masked figures holding an Antifaschistische Aktion banner near a fire line, an Instagram account (antidote503), a tweet from @InteriorCrocodileAlligator mocking claims that antifa started the fires, a citation/ticket, a kerosene-can shopping listing, a news headline about power poles cut with a chainsaw in Snohomish County, Google Street View shots of a house, vehicles, a police-stop photo, an Oregon license plate number, and images of Oregon ID cards. The collage asserts a real name, street address, and birthdates for the man; those personal identifiers are withheld here.
